title: Has science made God unnecessary? · Apologetics · Bible Guide
heading: Has science made God unnecessary?
paragraph: Learning how a natural process works does not remove its dependence on God. Scripture presents creation as declaring his glory and Christ as sustaining all things. God's works and his Word cannot ultimately contradict, though our scientific models and biblical interpretations can be mistaken.

blocks.text: The world we investigate is sustained by its Creator.

Learning how a natural process works does not remove its dependence on God. Scripture presents creation as declaring his glory and Christ as sustaining all things. God's works and his Word cannot ultimately contradict, though our scientific models and biblical interpretations can be mistaken.
R. C. SproulThe unity of truth and fallible interpretation
From the claim to the conclusion.
Creation is a witness to God rather than a realm independent of him.
God ordinarily works through means without being confined to them.
Finding an ordinary cause does not establish that nature is all that exists.
R. C. SproulNature and its divine author
Scientific inquiry can describe God's world; it cannot make that world self-sufficient simply by describing it.
God is more than a placeholder

Do not build a case on a temporary gap in knowledge. The biblical Creator governs what we understand as well as what we do not. Greater knowledge of creation can deepen gratitude rather than push God into a smaller corner.
R. C. SproulThe unity of truth

Identify the biblical text, the interpretation being proposed and the scientific claim. Scripture remains our final authority; an interpretation can need correction without God's Word being false. This guide does not adjudicate particular measurements or theories.
R. C. SproulScripture, science and interpretation
Does faith require us to ignore evidence?
No. God's works declare his glory. We should investigate truthfully while recognising that human judgments remain fallible and that neither a model nor a private interpretation has God's authority.
R. C. SproulInterpreting nature and Scripture
The distinction between Creator and creation does not settle a disputed scientific claim. Do not present a conclusion about biology or cosmology as if it followed merely from a Bible reference.
R. C. SproulDistinguishing truth from our interpretations
Which finding seems to conflict with which passage, and what assumptions connect the two?
